service.description: Internal, from ensure#CaseProfile: a new case's clocks, once. The organization's policy whose conditions hold at the accepted intake time, the most specific first (a service agreement, the customer, the queue, the type, the default), and its target for the case's priority band; a first response and a first resolution episode bound to that row, target and calendar (the policy's, else the queue team's working hours), with their due and warning times in business time; the case's due date becomes the resolution due date. With no policy it records that and leaves the case's due date. No permission: every entry point gets its clocks.

Internal, for the rules of entity/Request.eecas.xml (D23), so every path records: kind status (a case's status, due date or resolution changed by any screen or service: the status event, and the clocks paused, resumed, met, reopened as a new resolution episode or cancelled; a due date written outside the service levels is recorded), message (a message filed on the case: an outward response its channel accepted meets first response, a customer's message is a reply) or work (work made or linked). Not a case: nothing. A failure is logged, never the change's.

A case's clocks and their events (design CaseDetail's clocks, CaseAnalytics CaseMetrics): each clock's state, start, due, warning and actual times in its zone, its elapsed and remaining business time, pauses and breach, and the policy row and calendar it was bound to; each event in order with its reason and who. A case of the user's organizations only (RECORD_UNAVAILABLE).

parameter.name: noPolicy
parameter.description: No policy applied to the case at intake

service.description: A manager's correction of a case clock's due date with a reason (REASON_REQUIRED, DUE_REQUIRED): an event keeps the earlier figure, a clock already ended is met or missed again by its actual time, and the case's due date follows its resolution clock. Needs SUPPORT_CASE_MANAGE and the case's organization (RECORD_UNAVAILABLE); refuses a cancelled case's clock (CLOCK_CANCELLED).

An organization's service level policies (SlaPolicyList), the most specific first: each row's conditions, rank, calendar, period and state (Draft, Scheduled, In effect, Ended: with includeEnded only), pauses, reopen and targets per priority band. Needs SUPPORT_POLICY_EDIT, SUPPORT_CASE_MANAGE or SUPPORT_CASE_EDIT and the organization.

A service level policy row (SlaPolicyEdit): new, from a date (now when not given) or as a draft (no from date); a draft changed or published; a published row replaced from a date (the new row names it, previousPolicyId, and it ends there with its targets); or ended (end). Its conditions: a service queue of the organization (QUEUE_UNAVAILABLE), a request type (TYPE_UNKNOWN), a customer it serves (CUSTOMER_UNAVAILABLE), a service agreement of the organization (AGREEMENT_UNAVAILABLE); its calendar the organization's or a team's (CALENDAR_UNAVAILABLE); its targets per priority band in whole business minutes, a warning before its target (TARGET_INVALID, TARGETS_REQUIRED). Refuses a published row with the same conditions as another over the same dates (EQUAL_RANK_OVERLAP). An episode keeps the row it began with. Needs SUPPORT_POLICY_EDIT and the organization.

parameter.name: targets
parameter.description: Maps of priorityBandEnumId, firstResponseMinutes, resolutionMinutes and warningMinutes; a band with neither target is left out

service.description: SlaSimulation: when a case received at receivedDate with a priority (or band) is due for first response and resolution on a policy (given, or the one a case of the organization, queue, type and customer would get), with the pauses given (resolution only), the warnings, the working hours and the holidays over the span, in the schedule's zone. Needs SUPPORT_POLICY_EDIT, SUPPORT_CASE_MANAGE or SUPPORT_CASE_EDIT and the organization.

parameter.name: simulation
parameter.description: configured, policyName, bandText, receivedText, timeZone, calendarText, hoursText, clocks (label, targetText, dueText, dueDate, warningText, pausedText), holidays (name, fromText, thruText) and explanation

service.description: The warning and breach scan (the scan_CaseSla ServiceJob): a bounded batch (limit, 200) of running clocks past their warning or due time not yet recorded, oldest due first, then in the rest of the batch the paused ones past their policy's longest pause not yet recorded; each in its own transaction (mark#CaseSlaEpisode): its breach or warning recorded once per episode and told on SupportCaseSlaBreach or SupportCaseSlaWarning, a pause past the policy's longest recorded. A clock that fails is logged with its case and named in failedList, and the rest go on.

parameter.name: failedList
parameter.description: Maps of requestId, caseSlaEpisodeId and message

service.description: Internal, for scan#CaseSla: one clock's breach, warning or long pause, once (by its event key), in the caller's new transaction.
